descriptions.text: This was a pricing/arbitrage exploit against Usual Money's USD0++ (USD0Plus) VaultRouter deposit flow combined with the USD0/USD0++ Curve pool. The attacker took a Morpho Blue flash loan of ~1.9M USD0++, deposited it through the VaultRouter's deposit() which performs a swap via ParaSwap/Augustus at a stale or mispriced sync-vault rate, then arbitraged the resulting tokens back and forth through the USD0/USD0++ Curve pool (exchange index 0 1) where the redemption/exchange rate was favorable relative to the deposit price. The mispricing between the vault's internal valuation and the Curve pool's market price let the attacker repay the flash loan and walk away with the spread, finally routing USD0 -> USDC -> WETH on Uniswap V3 for ~$43K profit. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x585d8be6a0b07ca2f94cfa1d7542f1a62b0d3af5fab7823cbcf69fb243f271f8 Analysis: BlockSec / QuadrigaInitiative post-mortem

According to monitoring by SlowMist, Usual Protocol suffered a sophisticated arbitrage attack. The attacker exploited a price discrepancy between the protocol’s internal mechanisms and external markets. The core issue lay in the Vault system, which allowed a fixed 1:1 exchange between USD0++ and USD0—despite the two tokens trading at different prices on decentralized exchanges. The attacker strategically created a custom liquidity pool and manipulated the transaction path to trick the Vault into releasing USD0 tokens without receiving the expected sUSDS collateral. Usual Protocol’s usUSDS++ vault on Ethereum was exploited on May 27, 2025, when a capped unwrap route allowed an attacker to earn roughly $43,000 through arbitrage. No user or protocol funds were drained, and automated monitoring paused the vault promptly after the exploit transaction. A behavioral vulnerability in the capped deposit/unwrap route of the usUSDS++ vault allowed repeated conversion from USD0++ to USD0 without strict input validation, enabling profitable arbitrage.
